evidence_quotes.section1_quid_pro_quo: Rep skips the time-boxed framing and does not use recognizable language about 10-15 minutes or waiting for a yes. Goes straight into 'Let me just run through the details.'
evidence_quotes.section1_discovery_basics: Moving day (Friday) clarified; route (3220 Bunker Hill Road to 3901 Dorchester Drive in Raleigh) confirmed; city-to-city route present; size not directly asked ('one bedroom' inferred from items, not from square footage or room-count question).
evidence_quotes.section2_their_agenda: Asked after probing has started. Rep says 'do you have any important concerns for this move that you also want to discuss on this call aside from the pricing' — but this comes after the customer has already mentioned specific details they want to give and clarified the move date.
evidence_quotes.section3_logistics: Gathered: items list (bed, dressers, TV stands, washer/dryer), parking details (front of house vs. alley), walking distance (30-40 feet), elevator access both locations. Missing: property type explicitly stated, floor/stories (inferred as apartment floor 4, but not asked as a structured question), additional rooms, special considerations probing.
evidence_quotes.section3_packing_services: Not asked in recognizable form. Rep says 'you'll handle the packing as well' — a statement, not an offer or question about packing services.
evidence_quotes.section4_estimate_anchor: Typical range given ($525–$735 estimated budget for 2.5–3.5 hours) and personalized to customer's items ('one bedroom worth of items'). Anchored and personalized both present.
evidence_quotes.section4_pricing_framing: Fee transparency present: trip fee/transportation fee mentioned as included; 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments explicitly stated. Both elements of pricing framing present.
evidence_quotes.section4_feels_fair: Not asked. Rep moves directly to 'Now that being said would you like our help for this move on Friday?' — no pause for reaction to pricing.
evidence_quotes.section5_on_time_guarantee: Fully delivered: 'if we run late, we provide discounts for your move' with discount framing clear.
evidence_quotes.section5_damage_coverage: Fully delivered: '$2,000 coverage for any accidental damages' with no deductible or fine-print language, and built into the rate (implied by 'all inclusive').
evidence_quotes.section5_closes_the_loop: No closing question asked. Rep moves directly to the explicit ask without a 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar.
evidence_quotes.section6_final_concerns_check: Asked as 'Any questions so far?' — a throwaway version, not genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.section7_explicit_ask: Fully plain: 'would you like our help for this move on Friday?' No soft-out built in.
evidence_quotes.section7_rate_lock: Mentioned: 'No deposit at this time. The payment is only upon completion of the move.'
evidence_quotes.section7_booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (Friday 8:30–9:00 AM), phone number (not explicitly in transcript, email sent), apartment number (2434), addresses implied. Missing: crew size, explicit arrival window confirmation, notes left for crew about customer concerns (washer/dryer addition was mentioned but not formally captured as a crew note).

top_strength: Joanna expertly gathered detailed logistics (parking, walking distance, elevator access, floor-by-floor placement) and delivered a clear, anchored estimate ($525–$735) with transparent pricing (2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, all-inclusive framing) that set confident expectations.
coaching_note: Open Section 1 with the full quid pro quo framing (time-boxed ask + promise of a dependable quote + explicit wait for yes) rather than jumping straight into probing; this is the highest-value single item in the call card and protects the structure of everything that follows.
